Name: Aaron Weber
Bio: Standup comedian based in Nashville, TN and a regular performer at the Grand Ole Opry — the youngest comic ever to perform in the Opry circle. Originally from Montgomery, Alabama, he graduated from Notre Dame before pursuing comedy full-time. Co-hosts The Nateland Podcast with Nate Bargatze and Brian Bates, and released his debut special "Signature Dish" (executive produced by Bargatze/Nateland Entertainment).

Name: Adam Sandler
Bio: Stand-up comedian, actor, and musician from Brooklyn, New York, raised in Manchester, New Hampshire, who joined Saturday Night Live as a cast member from 1990 to 1995. Known for his everyman comic persona and novelty songs like "The Chanukah Song," he became one of Hollywood's biggest comedy stars with films including Billy Madison, Happy Gilmore, and The Wedding Singer, later earning acclaim for dramatic turns such as Uncut Gems. After decades away from the stage, he returned to stand-up with two Netflix specials, 100% Fresh (2018) and Love You (2024), and received the Kennedy Center's Mark Twain Prize for American Humor in 2023.

Name: Akaash Singh
Bio: Stand-up comedian and podcaster based in New York City, originally from Dallas, Texas. He left the pre-med track at Austin College to pursue comedy full-time, later breaking through with appearances on MTV's Wild 'n Out and Guy Code. Known for a brash, culturally pointed, crowd-work-heavy style, he built a large following co-hosting the Flagrant podcast alongside Andrew Schulz and self-releases his specials directly to YouTube, including Bring Back Apu (2022) and Gaslit (2024).

Name: Andrew Schulz
Bio: Stand-up comedian, actor, and podcaster who grew up in Manhattan's East Village and is now based in New York City. He graduated from UC Santa Barbara before building an early following through self-released, independently distributed specials on YouTube. Known for sharp, unfiltered observational and political comedy, he's since headlined sold-out arena tours and released the Netflix specials Schulz Saves America (2020) and Life (2025), along with the self-released Infamous (2022) — one of YouTube's most-watched comedy specials. Co-hosts the podcasts Flagrant with Akaash Singh and The Brilliant Idiots with Charlamagne Tha God.

Name: Anita Renfroe
Bio: Standup comedian and musical-comedy performer originally from Atlanta, Georgia and now based in the Texas Hill Country. Best known for her viral 2007 video "The Mom Song," a rapid-fire recitation of everyday mom phrases set to the William Tell Overture, she built her career on the Christian and family-friendly comedy circuit, touring for years with the Women of Faith conference. Known for clean, music-driven comedy about marriage and motherhood, she's released numerous comedy DVDs and books, including Total Momsense and Don't Say I Didn't Warn You: Kids, Carbs, and the Coming Hormonal Apocalypse.

Name: Anjelah Johnson-Reyes
Bio: Stand-up comedian and actress born and raised in San Jose, California. Before comedy, she was an NFL cheerleader for the Oakland Raiderettes, earning Rookie of the Year honors and performing at Super Bowl XXXVII, before relocating to Los Angeles in 2005 to pursue comedy full-time. She rose to fame on MADtv, best known for character-based sketches like "Bon Qui Qui" and her nail salon bits, and has since released seven stand-up specials, including Say I Won't (2023) and Technically Not Stalking (2024), plus the podcast Funjelah.

Name: Bert Kreischer
Bio: Stand-up comedian and podcaster born in St. Petersburg, Florida and raised in Tampa, who spent six years at Florida State University and became the subject of a notorious 1997 Rolling Stone profile chronicling a college trip to Russia — the origin of his signature story and nickname, "The Machine," later adapted into a 2023 action-comedy film of the same name. Known for shirtless, high-energy storytelling built around outrageous personal anecdotes, he's released stand-up specials for Comedy Central and Netflix, including Secret Time (2018), Hey Big Boy (2020), and Razzle Dazzle (2023). Co-hosts the podcast 2 Bears, 1 Cave with Tom Segura and produces his own show, Bertcast.

Name: Bill Cosby
Bio: Stand-up comedian and storyteller from Philadelphia, PA, who served in the U.S. Navy before earning degrees from Temple University and UMass Amherst. He began performing in Philadelphia and New York clubs in the early 1960s, building his reputation on observational, conversational storytelling about childhood and family life rather than topical material. He holds the record for the most Grammy Awards for Best Comedy Album and is closely associated with the animated series Fat Albert and the Cosby Kids, which he created, and the sitcom The Cosby Show. His concert film Bill Cosby: Himself (1983) is widely regarded as one of the most influential stand-up specials ever made.

Name: Bill Engvall
Bio: Stand-up comedian and actor originally from Galveston, Texas, now based in Park City, Utah. Best known for his signature "Here's Your Sign" bit, he co-founded the Blue Collar Comedy Tour in 2000 alongside Jeff Foxworthy, Larry the Cable Guy, and Ron White. Created and starred in The Bill Engvall Show (2007–2009) and later joined the cast of Last Man Standing. Built a decades-long stand-up catalog anchored by his platinum-certified debut album Here's Your Sign (1996), and closed out his touring career with the farewell special Here's Your Sign, It's Finally Time — My Last Show (2023).

Name: Jeff Foxworthy
Bio: Stand-up comedian born and raised near Atlanta, Georgia, who spent five years in mainframe computer maintenance at IBM before winning Atlanta's Great Southeastern Laugh-Off in 1984 and turning to comedy full-time. Best known for his "You Might Be a Redneck If…" one-liners and as a founding member of the Blue Collar Comedy Tour alongside Larry the Cable Guy, Bill Engvall, and Ron White, he's billed as the largest-selling comedy-recording artist in history. Beyond stand-up, he's hosted the game show Are You Smarter Than a 5th Grader? and written the autobiography No Shirt, No Shoes… No Problem!, and continues to tour behind his latest special, The Joke's On Me (2026).

Name: Bob Saget
Bio: Stand-up comedian, actor, and director born in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, best known to mainstream audiences as wholesome single dad Danny Tanner on Full House and as the original host of America's Funniest Home Videos. Behind that squeaky-clean TV image, he built a parallel career as an unapologetically raunchy stand-up comic, a contrast he leaned into throughout his live shows and specials including That's What I'm Talkin' About (2013, Grammy-nominated) and Zero to Sixty (2017). He also hosted the podcast Bob Saget's Here For You. He died on January 9, 2022, at age 65, while on a stand-up tour.

Name: Brad Stine
Bio: Stand-up comedian and actor based near Nashville, TN, raised in Bremen, Indiana. Nicknamed "God's Comic" after an 8-page New Yorker profile, he's built a three-decade career on a rapid-fire, politically conservative and Christian-inflected comedic style taking aim at political correctness and cancel culture. He's released numerous stand-up specials and DVDs, including Tolerate This!, Wussification, and his most recent, Laugh While It's Legal (2025), and hosts the podcast Brad Stine Has Issues.

Name: Brad Williams
Bio: Stand-up comedian from Orange County, California, based in the Los Angeles area, born with achondroplasia (a form of dwarfism), which is central to his self-deprecating comedic style. He got his start at 19 when Carlos Mencia pulled him onstage during a live show, and went on to become the first stand-up comedian to headline a Cirque du Soleil production, "Mad Apple," in Las Vegas. He's released multiple one-hour specials — most recently Starfish (2023) and Live On Short Street (2026) — appeared in Netflix's stand-up showcase The Degenerates (2018), and co-hosts the podcast Heightened Babble with JB Ball.

Name: Bron Lewis
Bio: Melbourne, Australia-based stand-up comedian and writer, and a former high school teacher before pursuing comedy full-time. Co-winner of the National Raw Comedy competition in 2022, she was nominated for the Melbourne International Comedy Festival's Best Newcomer award in 2023 following her sold-out debut show, Probably. She's a writer for The Project and a regular panellist on Have You Been Paying Attention?, and her stand-up frequently draws on her life as a mother of three navigating parenting and everyday absurdities, most recently in her specials Obviously (2024) and Who's Talking?! (2025).

Name: Chad Daniels
Bio: Stand-up comedian and Minnesota native who still bases himself in his hometown of Fergus Falls. He got his start in 1998 at open-mic nights at ACME Comedy Company in Minneapolis, developing a deadpan, self-deprecating style built on dry Midwestern humor about marriage, fatherhood, and small-town life. Three of his comedy albums have cracked the Billboard comedy top 10, and he's one of only 13 comics ever to appear on The Tonight Show with Conan O'Brien. He co-hosts the podcasts Pretend Problems and Middle of Somewhere, and released his Netflix debut special, Empty Nester, in 2024.

Name: Chonda Pierce
Bio: Stand-up comedian based near Nashville, Tennessee, known as comedy's "Queen of Clean" for her family-friendly, faith-rooted humor. Born in Covington, Kentucky and raised in South Carolina as a preacher's daughter, she got her start at Nashville's Opryland Theme Park before building a solo career that made her the RIAA's top-selling female comedian of all time, with 14 gold/platinum-certified DVDs. She's been openly candid about her struggles with depression, chronicling the deaths of her mother and husband in the 2015 documentary Chonda Pierce: Laughing in the Dark, and has founded Branches Recovery Center to provide counseling for depression, anxiety, and addiction.

Name: Chris D'Elia
Bio: Stand-up comedian and actor known for his animated, character-driven delivery, with a career breakout as Danny Burton on NBC's Undateable and a memorable arc on Comedy Central's Workaholics. Born in Montclair, New Jersey and raised largely in Los Angeles, he briefly attended NYU before leaving to pursue comedy, performing his first stand-up set in 2006. He's released five one-hour specials — including Incorrigible (2015), Man on Fire (2017), and Grow or Die (2023) — and hosts the long-running podcast Congratulations with Chris D'Elia.

Name: Christina P
Bio: Stand-up comedian and podcaster born in Windsor, Ontario, Canada, and raised largely in Southern California. Known for a blunt, high-energy delivery tearing into marriage, motherhood, and aging, she came up through LA comedy clubs before headlining nationally. She co-hosts the long-running Your Mom's House podcast with her husband, comedian Tom Segura, and has released two Netflix hour specials, Mother Inferior (2017) and Mom Genes (2022).

Name: Christopher Titus
Bio: Stand-up comedian known for what he calls "hard funny" — unflinchingly dark, autobiographical material drawn from a turbulent upbringing, including an alcoholic father and a mother who died by suicide. Born in Castro Valley, California, his one-man show Norman Rockwell is Bleeding became the basis for the FOX sitcom Titus (2000–2002), which he starred in, co-created, and executive produced. One of stand-up's most prolific special-makers, he's self-released a new hour-plus special almost every year since 2004, including Neverlution, Angry Pursuit of Happiness, and 2024's Carrying Monsters, his tenth.

Name: Daniel Sloss
Bio: Scottish stand-up comedian from Fife, who began performing as a teenager and became one of the youngest comedians to headline a solo season at London's Soho Theatre and in the West End. Known for dark, brutally honest, deeply personal storytelling, he built an international following through the Netflix specials DARK and Jigsaw (both 2018) and the HBO special X (2019). He's since self-released further acclaimed specials directly through his own website, including SOCIO (2022), HUBRIS (2024), and CAN'T (2025).

Name: Daren Streblow
Bio: Stand-up comedian and radio host based in Minnesota, known for clean, family-friendly observational comedy in the style of Brian Regan and Jerry Seinfeld. Originally from Ely, Minnesota, he started in radio as a teenager before turning to stand-up in 1995 at Acme Comedy Company in Minneapolis, going full-time by 1998. He hosts the nationally syndicated Daren Streblow Comedy Show, airing in over 70 radio markets, and has released two hour-long specials through Dry Bar Comedy: Organic and Inorganic Life (2019) and Wives Talk Too Much (2020).

Name: Drew Lynch
Bio: Stand-up comedian best known for finishing runner-up on America's Got Talent Season 10 (2015), where Howie Mandel awarded him the Golden Buzzer. Originally from Indianapolis, Indiana, he developed a neurogenic stutter at age 20 after being struck in the throat by a softball, and turned to stand-up as part of his recovery, building a self-deprecating act around the stutter itself. He also hosts the long-running YouTube series Dog Vlog (starring his service dog, Stella) and the podcast Did I Stutter?!, and has released several hour-long specials distributed free on his own YouTube channel, including Concussed (2021) and The Stuttering Comedian (2025).

Name: Dustin Nickerson
Bio: Stand-up comedian based in San Diego, California, known for clean, family-friendly comedy centered on marriage, parenting, and domestic life. Originally from the Seattle, Washington area, he graduated from the University of Washington before building a following through clubs, colleges, and the Christian-comedy circuit. His debut special, Overwhelmed (2020), became one of Amazon Prime Video's highest-rated comedy specials, and he's since released additional specials including It Runs in the Family (2023). He co-hosts the podcast Don't Make Me Come Back There with his wife, Melissa, which joined Nate Bargatze's Nateland Podcast Network in 2024.

Name: Gabriel Iglesias
Bio: Stand-up comedian and actor who grew up in Long Beach, California, known worldwide by the nickname "Fluffy" — coined from an early bit about his weight ("I'm not fat, I'm fluffy") that became his signature brand. His act blends storytelling, sound effects, and character voices, and he's become one of the highest-grossing touring comedians in the world, making history in 2022 as the first comic to headline and sell out a Major League Baseball stadium (Dodger Stadium). He's released numerous Netflix specials, including I'm Sorry for What I Said When I Was Hungry (2016), Stadium Fluffy (2022), and Legend of Fluffy (2025), and starred in the Netflix sitcom Mr. Iglesias (2019–2020).

Name: Gina Brillon
Bio: Stand-up comedian and actress raised in the Bronx, New York, of Puerto Rican descent, who began performing at 17 after her mother entered her and her twin sister in a local comedy contest. She became the first Latina to win NBC's Stand Up for Diversity showcase in 2012, and in 2021 made history as the first Latina comedian to reach the finals of America's Got Talent (Season 16). Known for a high-energy, story-driven style rooted in her New York upbringing, she's released four one-hour specials, including The Floor Is Lava (2020, Gracie Award winner) and Mind Your Business (2025).

Name: Greg Davies
Bio: Stand-up comedian and actor from Wem, Shropshire, England, who worked as a secondary school drama teacher for roughly 13 years before turning to comedy full-time. Known for his towering 6'8" frame, often used as a comedic device, and a loud, exasperated stage persona, he's widely recognized for playing Mr. Gilbert in The Inbetweeners and for hosting the BAFTA-winning panel show Taskmaster since 2015. His stand-up work includes the Edinburgh Comedy Award-nominated debut Firing Cheeseballs at a Dog, The Back of My Mum's Head, and the Netflix special You Magnificent Beast.

Name: Henry Cho
Bio: Korean-American stand-up comedian born and raised in Knoxville, Tennessee, best known for pairing his Southern drawl with his Korean heritage. He attended the University of Tennessee before breaking into comedy in 1986, going on to national television appearances including The Tonight Show. A committed clean comic who works without profanity, he's performed at the Grand Ole Opry more than 100 times and in 2023 became the first Asian-American inducted as an Opry member. His filmed special, Henry Cho: What's That Clickin' Noise? (2006), aired on Comedy Central and later streamed on Netflix.

Name: Iliza Shlesinger
Bio: Stand-up comedian raised in Dallas, Texas, who trained with ComedySportz before attending Emerson College in Boston. In 2008 she became the first woman — and the youngest ever — to win NBC's Last Comic Standing, building a career on sharp observational humor about dating, womanhood, and generational identity. She's released seven stand-up specials, six for Netflix (including War Paint, Elder Millennial, and Hot Forever) plus 2025's A Different Animal for Amazon Prime, and hosts the podcast Ask Iliza Anything.

Name: JB Ball
Bio: Stand-up comedian and TV/sketch writer from Tampa, Florida, who has also worked as a segment producer on Kevin Hart's Ridiculousness and toured as an opener for Hart. Named 2014's "Florida's Funniest Comedian" and a 2016 Just For Laughs Montreal "New Faces" showcase pick, his comedy is billed as deceptively edgy and intelligent, mining humor from controversial and topical subjects. He co-hosts the podcast Heightened Babble with Brad Williams, and has released two hour-long specials, It's My Privilege (2023) and Jesus in the Crackhouse (2025).

Name: Jack Whitehall
Bio: British comedian, actor, and writer born in London, part of a comedy dynasty — his father, Michael Whitehall, is a recurring on-screen foil throughout his career. Known for his posh, self-deprecating persona, he co-wrote and starred as Alfie Wickers in the BBC sitcom Bad Education, and found crossover success with the Netflix travel series Jack Whitehall: Travels with My Father. He's released multiple Netflix stand-up specials, including At Large (2017), I'm Only Joking (2020, filmed at Wembley Stadium), and Settle Down (2024, filmed at London's O2 Arena).

Name: James Acaster
Bio: Stand-up comedian from Kettering, Northamptonshire, England, who played drums in local bands before turning to comedy full-time in 2008. Known for a surreal, absurdist, and meticulously structured storytelling style, he holds the record for the most consecutive Best Comedy Show nominations at the Edinburgh Fringe (five, 2012–2016) and became a familiar panel-show face on Mock the Week and Would I Lie to You?. His Edinburgh material was reworked into Netflix's four-part special series Repertoire (2018), and he co-hosts the hit podcast Off Menu with Ed Gamble.

Name: Jeff Allen
Bio: Clean, family-oriented stand-up comedian born in Sauk Village, Illinois, who began performing in Chicago comedy clubs in 1978. Sober since 1987 and a born-again Christian since 1997, he built his act around his "Happy Wife, Happy Life" philosophy, mining his own marriage, family, and faith struggles for material. He's released multiple Dry Bar Comedy specials with a claimed 400+ million combined video views, and authored the memoir Are We There Yet?: My Journey from a Messed-Up to Meaningful Life.

Name: Jeff Dye
Bio: Stand-up comedian and actor from the Seattle, Washington area, known for a charming, goofy crowd-work style. He broke through nationally in 2008 as a finalist on NBC's Last Comic Standing season 6, and later hosted MTV's Money From Strangers and Fox's Who the Bleep Is That? (2023). His stand-up work includes the special How I See It (2022) and his debut full-hour video special The Last Cowboy in LA (2024), produced with 800 Pound Gorilla Records.

Name: Jen Brister
Bio: British stand-up comedian based in Brighton, a fixture on the UK circuit since the mid-1990s and a regular panelist on Mock the Week and Live at the Apollo. Openly gay, she is mother to twin sons with her partner Chloe Martin, conceived via IVF — a subject she mines heavily in her stand-up alongside queer family life, marriage, and aging. Her stand-up hours include Meaningless (2018), Under Privilege (2019), and The Optimist (released as a filmed special in 2023), and she co-hosts the podcasts Memory Lane and Women Talking Bollocks.

Name: Jim Gaffigan
Bio: Stand-up comedian and actor known for clean, self-deprecating, food-obsessed observational comedy, including his signature bit voicing an imagined audience member reacting to his own jokes. Raised in Chesterton, Indiana, he moved to New York City in 1990 to pursue comedy after working in advertising by day and taking acting classes at night. He's released more than a dozen hour-long specials over two decades, co-created and starred in the semi-autobiographical The Jim Gaffigan Show (TV Land, 2015–2016), and is a bestselling author of humor books including Dad Is Fat (2013), drawing heavily on his life as a father of five.

Name: Jimmy Carr
Bio: Stand-up comedian known for rapid-fire, dark, taboo-skirting one-liners and his distinctive laugh. Born in Isleworth, London and raised in Buckinghamshire, he graduated from Cambridge and worked as a marketing executive before leaving corporate life around 2000 to pursue comedy full-time. Long-running host of the panel show 8 Out of 10 Cats (2005–2021) and its Countdown spin-off, he's toured continuously for two decades and released numerous filmed specials, including four for Netflix: Funny Business, The Best Of, Ultimate, Gold, Greatest Hits, His Dark Material, and Natural Born Killer.

Name: Jo Koy
Bio: Filipino-American stand-up comedian and actor raised by his single mother, Josie, in Tacoma, Washington, after spending part of his childhood in the Philippines. Much of his act centers on stories about his mom and his son, and he's built a reputation as one of the biggest live draws in comedy — in 2024 he set the record for most sold-out headlining shows by a comedian at the Kia Forum in Los Angeles. His 2020 Netflix special In His Elements was filmed on location in Manila, spotlighting Filipino culture and performers, and he starred in the 2022 film Easter Sunday.

Name: John Branyan
Bio: Veteran clean and Christian-circuit stand-up comedian, performing since the early 1990s, best known for a mock-Shakespearean rendition of The Three Little Pigs — a viral routine adapted into the book A Triune Tale of Diminutive Swine — along with a companion Goldilocks bit in the same style. He's released multiple stand-up specials through Dry Bar Comedy drawing heavily on family life and parenting material, and he and his wife, Lori, have four children and eleven grandchildren.

Name: John Crist
Bio: Stand-up comedian from Lilburn, Georgia, best known for viral Christian-culture and observational sketch videos, including "Every Parent at Disney" and "Christian Music: How It's Made," that have amassed over a billion combined views. A graduate of Samford University, he broke out through the Christian comedy circuit before relocating to Nashville, Tennessee, where he now bases his touring career. He hosts the podcast Net Positive with John Crist and has released four full-length stand-up specials, most recently Emotional Support (2025), and authored the 2022 book Delete That (and Other Failed Attempts to Look Good Online).

Name: John Mulaney
Bio: Stand-up comedian, writer, and actor originally from Chicago, Illinois, who graduated from Georgetown University before moving to New York to pursue comedy full-time. Rose to prominence as a Saturday Night Live writer from 2008 to 2013, co-creating the recurring character Stefon with Bill Hader, and later brought his meticulously written, storytelling-driven stand-up to Broadway with Oh, Hello alongside longtime friend and fellow Georgetown alum Nick Kroll. Built his reputation through a string of acclaimed Netflix specials, winning multiple Emmy Awards for his comedy writing, and currently creates, hosts, and executive produces the Netflix live variety talk show Everybody's Live with John Mulaney.

Name: Jonnie W
Bio: Clean comedian based in Nashville, Tennessee, known for blending storytelling, off-beat stand-up, and live music into his act. He got his start as a Young Adults Pastor at church before transitioning to comedy full-time, and has since toured 48 states — comedy clubs, churches, corporate events, and leadership conferences — and opened for Nate Bargatze on his Be Funny and Big Dumb Eyes arena tours. He's performed on the Grand Ole Opry's Circle Network and co-hosts the podcast Talk About That with John Driver.

Name: Jose Sarduy
Bio: Stand-up comedian and U.S. Air Force veteran (Lieutenant Colonel) best known for blending military stories with comedy about his Cuban-American upbringing. Born in Las Tunas, Cuba, he was brought to Miami as a young child via the Mariel boatlift, and later became a combat pilot at the U.S. Air Force Academy, serving in Operations Enduring Freedom and Iraqi Freedom. He began performing stand-up while still on active duty, going on to win the Rocky Mountain Laugh Off (2011), and has released two Dry Bar Comedy specials, Cuban Pilot and The Whitest Cuban You've Ever Seen.

Name: Josh Blue
Bio: Stand-up comedian born in Cameroon and raised in Saint Paul, Minnesota, known for his self-deprecating comedy about living with cerebral palsy. Won Season 4 of NBC's Last Comic Standing in 2006, which launched his career as a full-time touring headliner, and before comedy competed on the U.S. Paralympic soccer team at the 2004 Athens Games. He's released a string of stand-up specials — including Sticky Change (2012), Delete (2016), and Freak Accident (2024) — and still performs 200+ shows a year.

Name: Josh Wolf
Bio: Stand-up comedian based in the Las Vegas area, where he holds a long-running residency at Jimmy Kimmel's Comedy Club. Originally from Boston, Massachusetts, he attended Trinity University before moving to Los Angeles to pursue comedy, becoming a longtime round-table regular on E!'s Chelsea Lately and After Lately. Known for road-tested, observational stand-up, he's released a string of one-hour specials including Father of the Year (2019) and Here for the Fun (2023), and co-hosts the podcast Hey Maaaan with his son, Jacob Wolf.

Name: K-Von
Bio: Half-Persian stand-up comedian and actor born in Reno, Nevada, to an Iranian immigrant father and an American mother, raised largely in Las Vegas. He graduated from the University of Nevada, Reno before pursuing comedy full-time, later appearing on MTV's Disaster Date and NBC's Last Comic Standing. Branding himself "the most famous half-Persian comedian," he's built a large following through prolific self-produced and self-released specials mining the culture clash between his Persian and Middle-American upbringing, and wrote and directed the comedic documentary Nowruz: Lost & Found.

Name: Kathleen Madigan
Bio: Stand-up comedian from the St. Louis, Missouri area, one of seven children in a large Irish Catholic family. Known for her dry, sarcastic, road-warrior style built on decades of relentless touring, she has the unique distinction of being both a contestant and a judge on NBC's Last Comic Standing, and has twice toured with the USO to entertain troops in Iraq and Afghanistan. She's released numerous specials over a 25+ year career — including Bothering Jesus (Netflix), Hunting Bigfoot, and The Family Thread (both Prime Video) — and hosts the podcast Madigan's Pubcast.

Name: Kelsey Cook
Bio: Stand-up comedian originally from Spokane, Washington, who began performing while a student at Washington State University before relocating to Los Angeles to pursue comedy full-time. Known for a confessional, self-deprecating style centered on dating, relationships, and family, she often traces her material back to being raised by an International Yo-Yo Champion father and a Professional Foosball World Champion mother. She's appeared multiple times on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon, co-hosts the podcast Pretend Problems with fellow comedian Chad Daniels, and has released two hour-long specials, The Hustler (2023) and Mark Your Territory (2025).

Name: Kenn Kington
Bio: Clean and Christian-comedy circuit stand-up comedian based in Kennesaw, Georgia, who has performed for over 30 years, including sets in more than 1,000 churches nationwide. Known for family- and faith-friendly storytelling humor about marriage, parenting, and everyday chaos, he's a frequently-played act on SiriusXM radio and has appeared on Comedy Central. His credits include two Netflix specials, the Dry Bar Comedy special Enjoying Chaos (2021), and the Amazon Prime special Wow Moments, which won a Golden Crown award.

Name: Kevin Hart
Bio: Stand-up comedian and actor born and raised in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, who built his reputation on high-energy, physically animated storytelling rooted in family and everyday-life material. He's widely regarded as one of the highest-grossing touring comedians in the world, having released a string of specials including Laugh at My Pain, Let Me Explain, and Irresponsible. Beyond stand-up, he starred in the Ride Along and Central Intelligence film franchises and hosts the sports interview series Cold as Balls, and founded the production company Hartbeat.

Name: Kevin James
Bio: Stand-up comedian and actor known as an "everyman" physical and observational comic. Born in Mineola, Long Island, New York, he broke out playing Doug Heffernan on the CBS sitcom The King of Queens (1998–2007) and became a box-office star with the Paul Blart: Mall Cop franchise. A frequent collaborator with Adam Sandler's Happy Madison Productions, he's appeared in films including Grown Ups and the Hotel Transylvania series. His stand-up specials include Sweat the Small Stuff (2001), the Netflix special Never Don't Give Up (2018), and the Prime Video special Irregardless (2024).

Name: Leanne Morgan
Bio: Stand-up comedian from East Tennessee known for her Southern, self-deprecating take on marriage, motherhood, and midlife. Before comedy, she spent years as a door-to-door jewelry saleswoman, where her jokes about family life with customers eventually led to paid comedy bookings — stardom didn't arrive until her late 50s. Her 2023 Netflix debut special, I'm Every Woman, became a breakout hit, followed by a second special, Unspeakable Things (2025), and she went on to co-create, executive produce, and star in Leanne, a Netflix sitcom based on her life.

Name: Matt Rife
Bio: Stand-up comedian and actor from Ohio who started performing at 14 and skipped college to pursue comedy full-time. He built an early national profile as a cast member on MTV's Wild 'n Out before a wave of viral TikTok clips of his crowd work turned him into one of the fastest-rising names in comedy, driving a record-breaking arena tour and sold-out shows at venues like Madison Square Garden. His 2023 Netflix debut special, Natural Selection, drew significant backlash for a joke referencing domestic violence, followed by a widely criticized mock apology; he's continued releasing crowd-work-focused specials on Netflix, including Lucid – A Crowd Work Special (2024) and Unwrapped (2025).

Name: Michael Ian Black
Bio: Stand-up comedian and actor raised in Hillsborough, New Jersey, who attended NYU's Tisch School of the Arts before leaving to join a Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles promotional tour. Got his start as a founding member of MTV's sketch troupe The State, later co-created and starred in Comedy Central's Stella, and became widely recognized for his dry, deadpan commentary on VH1's I Love the 80s. A prolific author of humor books and memoirs, he's also known for playing McKinley in Wet Hot American Summer and its Netflix follow-ups, and has released stand-up specials including Very Famous (2011) and Noted Expert (2016).

Name: Michael Jr
Bio: Clean and faith-based stand-up comedian and "comedic thought leader" known for using comedy as a bridge to purpose and deeper conversation, with material designed to work equally in comedy clubs and churches. He rose to wider prominence via his TEDx talk "More Than Funny," which uses the structure of a comedic setup and punchline as a metaphor for life purpose and has drawn millions of views on YouTube. He's appeared on The Tonight Show and Jimmy Kimmel Live!, starred in the 2020 faith-based film Selfie Dad, and authored the book Funny How Life Works.

Name: Michael McIntyre
Bio: Stand-up comedian and television presenter from London, England, known for observational comedy about everyday domestic minutiae and relatable family life. One of the UK's best-selling live comedians, he's sold over 4 million tour tickets and holds the record for most sold-out shows at London's O2 Arena. He hosts the BBC One series Michael McIntyre's Big Show and The Wheel, and broke through nationally after a standout performance at the 2006 Royal Variety Performance. His work includes multiple bestselling DVD releases, the 2020 Netflix special Showman, and two memoirs, Life & Laughing and A Funny Life.

Name: Mike Birbiglia
Bio: Stand-up comedian and storyteller from Shrewsbury, Massachusetts, who graduated from Georgetown University in 2000 before moving to New York to pursue comedy full-time. Known for long-form storytelling comedy that blends stand-up with theater, much of his material centers on his REM sleep behavior disorder — including the real-life incident in which he sleepwalked and ran through a second-story hotel window. A regular contributor to NPR's This American Life, he's turned six one-man shows into Netflix specials, including Sleepwalk with Me, The New One, and The Old Man & The Pool, several of which also ran on and off Broadway.

Name: Nate Bargatze
Bio: Stand-up comedian raised in the Old Hickory neighborhood of Nashville, Tennessee, known for a clean, deadpan, everyman storytelling style built around rambling, hyper-specific tangents about family and daily life. He cut his teeth in NYC clubs in the mid-2000s before breaking through nationally via his 2017 episode of Netflix's The Standups, followed by the specials The Tennessee Kid (2019) and the Grammy-nominated The Greatest Average American (2021). He's become one of the highest-grossing arena and stadium comedians in the world, has twice hosted Saturday Night Live, and in 2023 founded the family-friendly production company Nateland Entertainment.

Name: Norm Macdonald
Bio: Stand-up comedian and actor born in Quebec City, Canada, best known for his deadpan, absurdist delivery and his run anchoring Saturday Night Live's Weekend Update from 1994 to 1998 — a tenure that ended abruptly amid his relentless O.J. Simpson jokes, which he long maintained got him fired. A beloved fixture of late-night and talk-show couches, he was known for meandering, shaggy-dog style storytelling with hosts like David Letterman and Conan O'Brien. His film work includes a starring role in the cult comedy Dirty Work (1998), and he authored the surreal, fact-bending memoir Based on a True Story: Not a Memoir (2016). He died in September 2021 after privately battling leukemia for nearly a decade, with a final special, Nothing Special, released posthumously on Netflix in 2022.

Name: Pete Holmes
Bio: Stand-up comedian and podcaster known for a goofy, high-energy, voice-heavy delivery, best known as host of the long-running interview podcast You Made It Weird. Born in Boston and raised in Lexington, Massachusetts in an evangelical Christian household, he originally planned to become a youth pastor before pursuing comedy; a painful divorce from his college girlfriend later became the basis for his semi-autobiographical HBO series Crashing (2017–2019), created with Judd Apatow. He's released a series of stand-up specials for Comedy Central and HBO, and has done extensive voice work on animated series including American Dad! and The Secret Life of Pets 2.
